## Cartagena: What to See in the Fortified Old Town

Cartagena on Colombia's Caribbean coast is known for its fortified walls, cobbled streets and houses with wooden balconies. **The best introductory route runs through the historic centre and Getsemaní neighbourhood**, with a separate trip recommended for the beach.

Cartagena's historic port occupied an important position within the Spanish colonial system. A network of forts and defences was built to protect the city. In 1984, the port, fortresses and monuments of Cartagena were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. The designation recognises an entire historic ensemble, not just individual attractive façades.

### Squares, Walls and Streets of the Historic Centre

Start your walk at the city gate, then continue to the central squares and little streets of the old neighbourhoods. Churches, stone buildings, shaded courtyards and colourful balconies can be found here. Centro and San Diego are particularly interesting and easy to explore on foot, with breaks during the hottest hours.

The city walls help visitors understand where the historic port stood in relation to the sea. San Felipe de Barajas Fortress also deserves attention. Visiting it involves travel time and walking across exposed areas in the sun. If military history interests you more than museums, devote a substantial part of the day to the fortifications.

### Getsemaní: A Separate Walk

Getsemaní is close to the fortified core. Its cityscape is different: street art, small squares, homes and public spaces. It is better to visit without a rigid timetable so you can appreciate the murals and local life. Ask permission before photographing people, and respect private courtyards as private spaces.

## Beaches: Cartagena, Rosario and Barú

City sightseeing and an excursion to the islands serve different purposes. Comfortable shoes are enough for a city walk, but **a day at sea requires its own transport plan**. The [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/) offer Caribbean scenery and marine relaxation, while [Barú Island](/colombia/place/baru-island/) is known for its beaches and coastal nature.

| Place | Reason to visit |
|---|---|
| Historic centre | Architecture and museums |
| Getsemaní | Neighbourhoods and art |
| Rosario | Boat excursion |
| Barú | Beach relaxation |

When choosing a sea excursion, confirm the specific beach, departure and return times, landing arrangements and what happens in rough seas. A mention of “islands” does not mean that every island in the archipelago will be visited. Avoid combining a boat excursion with an international flight on the same day.

## How Many Days to Spend in Cartagena

One full day allows you to walk through historic neighbourhoods and see some of the fortifications. For a more relaxed visit, **2–3 nights** are convenient, especially if you want time for museums, Getsemaní and a separate sea excursion. City walks are usually more comfortable in the morning and towards evening than under the midday sun.

If you are travelling via [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) and [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), allow time for domestic transfers, changing climate and hotel check-in. Cartagena is considerably warmer than the high-altitude capital. In the [Colombia tours catalogue](/colombia/tour/), compare itineraries by nights and actual included visits, not just city names.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Cartagena

### What does the UNESCO designation cover?

Cartagena's historic port, fortifications and group of monuments. The site was inscribed in 1984 for the outstanding heritage of a fortified colonial city.

### Can I visit the Rosario Islands in one day?

Yes. One-day boat excursions are available. Timings and conditions depend on the particular island, weather, pier and transport. Confirm the landing point and return schedule in advance.

### Which should I choose: Cartagena or Medellín?

Cartagena's main attractions are the historic port and Caribbean Sea. [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) offers a modern Andean city, art and mountain surroundings. The two places reveal different aspects of Colombia.

## Tours via Cartagena: Choosing a Colombia and Caribbean Coast Itinerary

**Cartagena is a useful stop on a journey as both a historic city and a departure point for the Caribbean islands.** One itinerary provides a sightseeing walk through the fortified city; another adds a day on the [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/); a third follows the city stay with several nights on [Barú Island](/colombia/place/baru-island/). These are different styles of travel, even though Cartagena features in all of them.

Our catalogue contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with a scheduled visit to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). These are journeys that actually pass through the city on their main route. For its history, neighbourhoods and fortresses, see the separate [Cartagena destination guide](/colombia/place/cartagena/). Below, we compare the itineraries themselves: time in the city, what comes before and after, and which format to choose.

### Which Itineraries Should You Compare First?

| Programme | Main difference |
|---|---|
| [Bogotá and Cartagena, 5 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-essential-5-days/) | 2 cities, Zipaquirá, a Rosario day |
| [Colombia in 7 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-7-days/) | Bogotá, Medellín, Guatapé, Cartagena |
| [Cities, coffee and Caribbean, 9 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-explorer-9-days/) | Coffee region between the cities |
| [VIP: Cartagena and Barú, 10 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/) | Coffee region, then island relaxation |
| [Group Colombia and Barú, 12 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-baru-beach-group-tour-12-days/) | City programme and several days on Barú |
| [Grand Colombia, 15 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-cartagena-medellin-rosario-islands-santa-marta/) | Coffee region and a four-day mountain trek |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_colombia_essential_5_days,tour_colombia_highlights_7_days,tour_colombia_explorer_9_days,tour_source_tur_v_kolumbiyu_na_10_dnej,tour_source_manyashchaya_kolumbiya_baru,tour_source_fantasticheskaya_kolumbiya}}

The choice depends on **time and physical demands**, not just the number of cities. The five-day journey covers fewer regions. The nine-day route adds a separate coffee experience. The fifteen-day programme requires preparation for an extended hike and must not be treated as simply a longer version of a city tour.

## If You Have 5–7 Days: Cartagena with Bogotá or Medellín

The [five-day “From the Andes to the Caribbean” programme](/colombia/tour/colombia-essential-5-days/) starts with [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), followed by [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/) and [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/). Travellers then fly to Cartagena, explore the historic centre and take a trip to the [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/) with a visit to Isla Grande the following day. This suits a first introduction to two very different parts of Colombia: the high-altitude capital and hot Caribbean coast.

The [seven-day tour via Cartagena](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-7-days/) adds [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) and a visit to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and [El Peñón Rock](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/). Cartagena includes the historic centre, San Felipe Fortress and La Popa convent; a separate day is spent on the Rosario Islands. This route involves more domestic travel but lets you compare the capital, the Andean region around Medellín and the coast in one week.

**How to choose:** Five days work if Bogotá and the Caribbean are your priorities, without adding another city. Seven days are worthwhile for Medellín and Guatapé. In both cases, check arrival and departure times: the first and last days are partly spent travelling. Also check whether domestic airfare is included in the particular rate. A flight listed on the itinerary is not necessarily included in the published price.

## Cartagena on 9–11-Day Routes: Adding Coffee or Islands

The [nine-day “Colombia in Four Chapters” tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-explorer-9-days/) links Bogotá, [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/), Medellín and Cartagena. In the coffee region, travellers visit [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/), [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/) and learn about coffee production. City sightseeing in Medellín and a trip to Guatapé follow, before a Caribbean finale on the Rosario Islands. This makes sense when coffee and mountain scenery matter as much as Cartagena.

The [ten-day VIP itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/) is different: Bogotá and the coffee region are followed by 2 nights in Cartagena and 3 nights on [Barú](/colombia/place/baru-island/). Cartagena's programme lists the Old Town, San Felipe and La Popa. The island stay is a separate part of the journey, not a few hours after city sightseeing. Check the exact hotels and services in the specific itinerary: the VIP label itself does not automatically include every possible personalised service.

On the [11-day “Complete Colombia” journey](/colombia/tour/colombia-complete-11-days/), the coffee region and Cartagena are followed by [San Andrés](/colombia/place/san-andres/), then Medellín. San Andrés is a separate Caribbean island and must not be confused with Barú or the Rosario archipelago. This is a different way to spread beach time across sightseeing days.

If visiting a coffee farm is your main goal, compare [coffee tours in Colombia](/interests/coffee-tours/tours/colombia/). Some itineraries include a farm as a substantial separate stage; others make coffee part of a broader cultural journey.

## Cartagena, Rosario and Barú: Three Different Travel Experiences

Cartagena primarily offers **a historic city programme**. Its fortifications, walls and colonial buildings are recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Walks through the old centre focus on architecture, squares, bastions and the port's history. Some itineraries include San Felipe de Barajas Fortress and La Popa convent. There is also a standalone [Cartagena city tour](/colombia/cartagena/cartagena-city-san-felipe-castle-tour/).

The [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/) involve a boat excursion that may occupy most of the day. Some of our programmes include relaxation on Isla Grande or San Pedro de Majagua. Plan for travel to the pier, boarding, island time and the return crossing. A separate option is the [Rosario Islands excursion from Cartagena](/colombia/rosario-islands/rosario-islands-tour-from-cartagena/).

[Barú Island](/colombia/place/baru-island/) serves a different purpose on itineraries that stay overnight: several days by the sea. For instance, the [12-day group tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-baru-beach-group-tour-12-days/) moves from Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena into several days of relaxation on Barú. For a genuine beach holiday, extra nights matter more than adding another sightseeing tour.

| Option | Why choose it |
|---|---|
| Cartagena | Architecture, history, city |
| [Rosario](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/) | Daytime boat excursion |
| [Barú](/colombia/place/baru-island/) | Beachfront stay with overnights |
| [San Andrés](/colombia/place/san-andres/) | Separate island stage |

These places complement one another but cannot be reduced to an interchangeable “beach programme”. Walking through the old town means hours on foot in the heat; a day at sea depends on weather and transport; staying several nights requires different luggage and accommodation arrangements.

## If You Want a Longer Route: Cartagena at the End

The [14-day Colombia tour](/colombia/tour/iconic-colombia-14-days/) visits Bogotá, Medellín, Pereira, a coffee farm and Cocora Valley before Cartagena. It then covers Cartagena sightseeing, the Rosario Islands and [Santa Marta](/colombia/place/santa-marta/) with [Tayrona Park](/colombia/place/tayrona-national-park/). This itinerary explores several regions rather than offering an extended stay in a single resort hotel.

An even more active option is the [15-day “Fantastic Colombia” tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-cartagena-medellin-rosario-islands-santa-marta/). It includes Bogotá, Medellín, the coffee region and a **four-day trek to the [Lost City](/colombia/place/ciudad-perdida/)** from the Santa Marta area, finishing in Cartagena and the Rosario Islands. Good physical fitness and readiness for several days of walking really matter. If trekking is not for you, choose an itinerary without it rather than trying to turn that section into a short bus excursion.

Other opportunities for history and the coast can be found in [Colombia cultural and historical tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/) and [Colombia beach programmes](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/colombia/). The themed selections contain different tours; verify the particular itinerary when Cartagena itself is important.

## Preparing for the Caribbean Part of the Journey

The coast is hot and humid. Light clothes, a hat, water and shoes comfortable for extended walks on stone streets are useful for daytime sightseeing. For boat excursions, bring sun protection, waterproof document storage and a time buffer before any evening flight. Boat schedules and safe conditions for sailing depend on weather and port restrictions.

If the itinerary includes Andean cities, prepare for a **change in climate**: Bogotá is much higher above sea level and considerably cooler than Cartagena. One clothing selection may not work for the entire trip. Domestic flights also deserve attention: routes and transfers may be listed in the itinerary while flight tickets themselves are excluded or sold under a separate rate.

Before booking, compare four things between the two programmes you like: the number of nights in Cartagena, whether and how the island day is included, flights included in the price, and the full list of excursions. That is more informative than the word “Caribbean” in a tour title.

## Questions About Tours Visiting Cartagena

### How much time should I allow for Cartagena on a tour?

A separate city excursion is usually planned for the historic centre and fortress; a programme with Rosario adds a distinct sea day. A stay on Barú needs several nights. Compare the [five-day](/colombia/tour/colombia-essential-5-days/) and [ten-day itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/): Cartagena serves different purposes in each.

### Is a Rosario Islands excursion included in every tour via Cartagena?

No. Cartagena appearing in an itinerary confirms the city visit, but the islands must be explicitly listed on a programme day. They are included, for example, in the [seven-day tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-7-days/) and [nine-day route](/colombia/tour/colombia-explorer-9-days/).

### Can I combine Cartagena and coffee plantations?

Yes. The [nine-day journey](/colombia/tour/colombia-explorer-9-days/) passes through the coffee region around Pereira, Salento and Cocora Valley before continuing to Medellín and Cartagena. A [VIP route with coffee and Barú](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/) is another option.

### Which should I choose for time by the sea: Rosario or Barú?

Rosario is convenient for a day trip by boat, while Barú is a better fit for an extended stay with overnights. Specific beaches and accommodation depend on the [Barú tour itself](/colombia/tour/colombia-baru-beach-group-tour-12-days/); one island day is not equivalent to several nights beside the sea.

### At what stage of the route is Cartagena usually visited?

On many itineraries, Cartagena comes after Bogotá, Medellín or the coffee region and serves as the Caribbean finale. But this is not universal: the [eleven-day itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-complete-11-days/) continues to San Andrés and Medellín after Cartagena. Check the daily order, not just the list of cities.

## Chicaque Park: Cloud Forest and Hiking Near Bogotá

**Chicaque is a place for walks through mountain mist, moss-covered trees and ferns.** The park lies in the hills near [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/). Even a short route is different from a city walk: wet roots and uneven ground may lie underfoot, and clouds drift down into the forest.

The park administration states that Chicaque has more than 20 km of ecological trails of varying difficulty. It is therefore better to select one or two routes before visiting rather than attempting to walk around the entire park in a day.

### Which Trails Should You Choose?

Marked routes include Colonial, the oak forest, the waterfall trail and the climb to Pico del Águila. They differ in physical effort and scenery.

| Trail | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Colonial | Historic forest road |
| Bosque de Robles | Oak forest section |
| Cascada | Waterfall and damp slopes |
| Pico del Águila | Mountain viewpoint |

The park describes the exertion level for each trail separately. A walk to the waterfall may require an extra climb on the way back; Pico del Águila includes more difficult stretches. When travelling with children or people with limited stamina, compare difficulty and duration rather than choosing by name.

### How to Judge Your Energy

**The entrance is in the upper part of the park, so the descent may seem easier than the return climb.** This is an important feature of Chicaque. Allow time and energy specifically for the way back, especially if walking to lower forest areas.

The park's official recommendations suggest sturdy grippy footwear, comfortable clothing, rain protection and a light backpack. Warm layers can also help in the damp and cool conditions. Stay on marked paths in poor visibility.

## What Can You See in the Cloud Forest?

Chicaque is home to moisture-loving plants: mosses, ferns, epiphytes and dense green vegetation. Various birds inhabit the forest, but sightings of particular species cannot be guaranteed. For wildlife watching, walk slowly, stop and listen rather than rushing constantly to the next point.

Some stretches open onto panoramas of the surrounding mountains. Visibility depends on cloud and weather. If a photograph from a high viewpoint is your main objective, allow flexibility to change the order of stops as the fog shifts.

The administration offers additional activities, including ziplining and horseback rides. Their availability in the park does not automatically mean they are included in a standard entrance ticket or any tour. Additional services must be confirmed separately.

## Visiting Chicaque from Bogotá

It is best to plan a dedicated day rather than treating the park as a short stop between museums. Driving time depends on where you leave Bogotá and traffic. Once there, allow for selecting a route, the walk itself and enough time to return.

To combine the city and nature on one trip, start by exploring [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) and dedicate another day to Chicaque. In the [Colombia tour catalogue](/colombia/tour/), check whether a park visit is specifically listed and what the programme includes.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Chicaque Park

### Can I visit Chicaque without a long hike?

Yes. The park has routes of varying difficulty, but the terrain is mountainous and even a short walk may include a significant climb on the way back.

### Do I need rain protection?

Yes. This is a humid cloud forest. Comfortable non-slip shoes and light waterproof clothing are useful even with a favourable forecast.

### Does park admission include ziplining?

Standard admission covers the grounds and trails. Extra activities must be checked and paid for according to the park's current terms.

## Tours via Chicaque Park: Choosing an Itinerary

[Chicaque Park](/colombia/place/chicaque-park/) lies near [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) and is known for humid mountain forest, trails among moss-covered trees and views from hillsides. An interesting aspect of travelling through Colombia is the opportunity to see the capital, Andean forest and the very different landscapes of the lowlands around La Macarena on a single trip.

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that include Chicaque as a scheduled stop. Among them is the [“Season of Colours: Bogotá, La Macarena and Caño Cristales in 8 Days” tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-cano-cristales-8-days/). This is a private itinerary with a dedicated visit to Chicaque, not merely the possibility of adding the park for a surcharge.

**The decision:** if you only want to see the cloud forest, consider the [standalone Chicaque excursion](/colombia/chicaque-park/chicaque-forest-walk/). If the capital and Colombia's remote natural regions both appeal, the multi-day tour combines these experiences in a single journey.

## Visiting Chicaque on the Eight-Day Journey

On the [eight-day Colombia itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-cano-cristales-8-days/), the first days take place in Bogotá. After exploring historic neighbourhoods, museums and Mount Monserrate, it is time for a day in the cloud forest.

The Chicaque trip includes private transport from Bogotá, a guided park walk with a specialist Spanish-speaking guide, park admission and a traditional lunch. About 6 hours are allocated to this outing. The route leads along mountain trails to a forest refuge, after which travellers return to their hotel in the capital.

The journey then continues to [La Macarena](/colombia/place/la-macarena/), with a flight, canoe travel along the [Guayabero River](/colombia/place/guayabero-river/) and walking routes near [Caño Cristales](/colombia/place/cano-cristales/). Chicaque is thus one part of a trip through several natural zones of Colombia, not a separate multi-day hike in the forest.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_colombia_cano_cristales_8_days}}

## Full Tour or One-Day Excursion?

| What you want | Suitable format |
|---|---|
| See only the cloud forest | [Chicaque excursion](/colombia/chicaque-park/chicaque-forest-walk/) from Bogotá |
| Combine forest and Caño Cristales | [Eight-day Colombia tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-cano-cristales-8-days/) |
| More time in the capital | [Tours via Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/tour/), checking city days |
| Compare different regions | [All Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/) |

The standalone [Chicaque walk](/colombia/chicaque-park/chicaque-forest-walk/) has its own description of duration, guiding and included services. It suits those already in Bogotá who do not plan to continue to La Macarena. On the eight-day route, the excursion is integrated with flights and transfers over several days.

The protected area offers additional activities, such as horseback riding, ziplining and other experiences. Availability of these services in the park **does not mean** they are included in our tour. The confirmed programme includes a guided walk; extra activities should be arranged separately.

## Trails and Physical Demands

Chicaque is a mountainous nature reserve with trails of varying difficulty. Descents and ascents through forest, damp sections and uneven surfaces are common. The park's official website describes routes to viewpoints, oak forest and a waterfall, but visiting each depends on the chosen trail and available time. Our programme includes a route to the forest refuge, and all the park's other attractions cannot automatically be added.

Bring shoes with non-slip soles, a lightweight raincoat, water and a small backpack. Even when Bogotá is dry, the cloud forest can be cooler and damper. If [trekking to Caño Cristales](/colombia/place/cano-cristales/) follows Chicaque, plan clothing for both environments: subsequent days also involve walking, but in a hotter and more open landscape.

The current tour description expressly states that Chicaque's uneven trails **are unsuitable for travellers with limited mobility**. Even if transport operates within the park, that does not make the included walking excursion barrier-free. To travel at a gentler pace, discuss a suitable level of exertion and exact route beforehand.

## How Chicaque Fits into the Rest of Colombia

The main feature of the multi-day itinerary is the contrast of experiences. [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) offers urban history, parks and museums. Chicaque reveals the Eastern Cordillera's cloud forest. [La Macarena](/colombia/place/la-macarena/) and [Caño Cristales](/colombia/place/cano-cristales/) bring rivers, aquatic plants, natural rock pools and walks in a different climate.

When choosing a programme, examine the order of stops as well as total days. Chicaque occupies its own day, and reaching the remote natural area involves a flight and further river and land journeys. If your main goal is to explore Chicaque leisurely, a standalone trip from the capital offers more freedom to choose forest trails. To see both natural areas on one journey, consider acceptable physical effort and the season of the principal excursion.

[Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/) can have very different priorities—the Caribbean coast, coffee region, mountain hikes or cultural routes. “Colombia” in the name does not guarantee a Chicaque stop: check its inclusion in the selected tour programme.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How much time does Chicaque take on the current tour?

About 6 hours are allotted to the excursion day including travel from Bogotá, walking in the park and returning. This is a confirmed feature of the [eight-day itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-cano-cristales-8-days/), not a recommended duration for visiting every park trail independently.

### Do I need to stay overnight in Chicaque?

On the specified itinerary, travellers return to Bogotá for the night. The park offers its own accommodation, but this is not part of the tour. Staying overnight would require a separately agreed itinerary change.

### Are a guide and park admission included?

Yes. The day includes a specialist Spanish-speaking guide, private transport, admission, walking and a traditional lunch. Guiding languages may differ on other parts of the trip; the full details appear on the tour page.

### Can I visit Chicaque without travelling to Caño Cristales?

Yes. There is a standalone [Chicaque Nature Park excursion from Bogotá](/colombia/chicaque-park/chicaque-forest-walk/). It focuses on cloud forest without a flight to La Macarena.

### When should I plan a trip via Chicaque?

Choose dates based on the trip's main goal. The route to Caño Cristales has its own season and flight logistics, while Chicaque lies in a different climate zone. Rain protection is needed for the hiking section at any time of year; check current opening hours and trail conditions before departure.

## Ciudad Perdida in Colombia: The Lost City and a Multi-Day Trek

**Ciudad Perdida**, also known as Teyuna, lies in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta mountains of northern [Colombia](/colombia/). This archaeological settlement is associated with the ancient Tairona culture. Circular stone terraces and staircases are surrounded by dense vegetation, and the only access is a long hiking trail.

Visiting here is completely different from an ordinary bus excursion. Travellers encounter not only the historic city but also mountain rivers, tropical forests and territories inhabited by Indigenous communities. The journey takes several days, requires physical preparation and must be organised with appropriate guides in advance.

## What Is the Ancient City of Teyuna?

Teyuna was founded long before the Spanish arrived in the region. Its archaeological remains include terraces, paved areas, stairways and traces of a complex settlement layout on mountain slopes. The circular foundations differ from the stepped pyramids of Central America. Many original buildings were made of materials that did not survive as well as the stone engineering works.

The site attracted archaeologists in the twentieth century after destructive treasure hunting by illegal looters of ancient graves. Its history of study includes damage to the heritage and subsequent preservation efforts. Seeing Ciudad Perdida only as a “secret place in the jungle” would therefore be unfair to the region's history.

Colombia's Institute of Anthropology and History, ICANH, is responsible for preserving the archaeological complex. The name Teyuna helps distinguish the historic place from the tourist marketing image of a “Lost City”.

## How to Reach Ciudad Perdida

[Santa Marta](/colombia/place/santa-marta/) is the departure city for most organised journeys. Travellers then transfer by road to the start of the walking route. From there, mountain trails are followed on foot, with stops and overnight stays in camps. There is no road for an ordinary vehicle directly to the ruins.

A typical programme takes **several days**. The current [Colombia itinerary covering Bogotá, Medellín, Cartagena and Santa Marta](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-cartagena-medellin-rosario-islands-santa-marta/) allocates four days to the Lost City trek. This duration applies to that particular product; other trekking options may have different daily distances, camps and conditions.

Independent hiking without an organised guide is not suitable here. ICANH describes access rules involving authorised routes and accompanying guides, while local communities play an important role in managing sacred territories. Before purchasing, ensure the operator is permitted to conduct trips on the route and that the chosen dates are open for visits.

## What Happens Along the Way?

### Tropical Forest and Mountain Rivers

The trail passes through hot, humid forest, crosses mountain streams and climbs hillsides. Ground and steps can become slippery after rain. Daily walks can combine extended ascents and descents in high humidity. Ordinary casual footwear and an insufficient supply of drinking water can therefore cause serious discomfort.

The nature of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta is valuable in itself. Yet the presence of birds and animals does not guarantee sightings of particular species, and difficulty should be assessed from elevation gain, weather and overall duration.

### Camps and Encounters with Local Culture

Multi-day programmes usually involve simple camp accommodation along the route. Sleeping arrangements, group sizes, meals and luggage transport may differ and should be checked for the specific programme rather than assumed.

The Sierra Nevada has cultural and spiritual significance to Indigenous communities. Photographing people, homes and ceremonies requires permission; being allowed into the region does not mean visitors can enter community or sacred spaces freely. Agreements with guides and respect for local rules are an essential part of the trek.

## How Difficult Is the Trek?

Teyuna requires the ability to walk for hours in a tropical climate. Conditions are much closer to genuine trekking than a city excursion. Expect steep steps, damp tree roots, river crossings and climbs in the sun. Backpack choice, footwear, water supply and rest arrangements noticeably influence the experience.

| Condition | What to consider |
| --- | --- |
| Duration | Several days with overnight stays |
| Terrain | Ascents, descents, steps |
| Climate | Heat, humidity, heavy rain |
| Access | Authorised hiking route with a guide |

This route is practically inaccessible to travellers with limited mobility: it is not suitable for wheeled transport and requires a substantial walk to the ruins. Anyone with serious health limitations should discuss participation with a medical professional and the organiser before paying.

## When to Plan the Trek and Check Park Opening

Weather in northern Colombia's mountains varies, and access depends on rain, trail conditions and decisions by the responsible authorities. Temporary restrictions may also result from conservation needs and the spiritual practices of Indigenous communities.

**Current update for October 2026:** ICANH announced that visits to Teyuna Park would resume on **16 October 2026**. Its 9 October decision revised an earlier closure plan running until 31 October: the actual closure lasted from 1 to 15 October. Current access conditions and specific dates still need to be verified before departure, while future seasons have separate schedules.

When planning, leave extra time for transport from Santa Marta and possible weather changes. Mobile coverage is limited along the route, so family or friends should know the departure and return dates, and communication with guides should be agreed in advance.

## Combining Ciudad Perdida, Tayrona and Santa Marta

[Tayrona National Park](/colombia/place/tayrona-national-park/) and the Teyuna archaeological park belong to the same broad mountainous coastal region but are **different sites with different routes and access rules**. A day on the Tayrona coast does not replace a hike to the ancient terraces of Ciudad Perdida.

Before or after the trek, spend time in [Santa Marta](/colombia/place/santa-marta/) and on the Caribbean coast. If the journey covers several Colombian regions, the mountain trek can be combined with cultural stops in [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) and [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). However, allow adequate recovery and rest after a physically demanding route.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Ciudad Perdida

### Can I drive to the Lost City?

No. A multi-day hiking trail leads to the ruins. Road vehicles can only reach the trailhead.

### How many days does the trek usually take?

It normally takes several days with overnight stays. One Ada Tours programme, for example, allocates four days. Exact duration depends on the route and tour conditions.

### Can I go without a guide?

Visits to the archaeological park must follow current access and guiding rules. Choose an authorised operator and check ICANH requirements before travelling.

### Is the Lost City in Tayrona National Park?

They are different visitor sites. Teyuna's archaeological complex is in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta mountains; Tayrona National Park has its own routes and access conditions.

### Is the Lost City open in October 2026?

According to ICANH's official announcement of 9 October 2026, visits resumed on 16 October after the closure from 1 to 15 October. Access and trail conditions should be checked again before the specific departure.
